fact: TechAfrica News reports that on the handover from KOICA in March 2026 NITDA took over the Nigeria Government Enterprise Architecture (NGEA) framework, built over two and a half years with reference models and described as now operational and enabling data exchange across government agencies; the event is dated by the article's publication date, 2026-03-27.
ThisDay reports that the Nigeria Governors' Forum's July 2025 report rated Katsina's policy alignment with the Nigeria e-Government Interoperability Framework (Ne-GIF) at high maturity.
NITDA's Director General, through a representative, said NITDA is developing a national interoperability framework and advancing Enterprise Architecture initiatives across government institutions.

NITDA issued the Nigeria e-Government Interoperability Framework (Ne-GIF), release v1.2 of August 2019 (v1.0 May 2018), under section 6(a) and (c) of the NITDA Act 2007, as the baseline framework for how MDAs' systems exchange data.
The Ne-GIF lists its enforcement category as Recommended, not Mandatory, and section 4.5 states that compliance cannot be compelled, only encouraged, and that enforceable guidelines are still needed.

NITDA issued the Nigerian Government Enterprise Architecture (NGEA) v1.0, status Released, March 2019, under the NITDA Act 2007, as a framework for all public institutions whose data reference model points to the Ne-GIF for data sharing and exchange.
The NGEA's document metadata lists its enforcement category as Recommended, and its sections 4.3 and 4.4 only encourage federal public institutions to set up EA teams and units.
